reason: The original says his shell came off in a hedge. The rewrite says it got stuck in a hedge and loses the shedding.
The original says the house shed. The rewrite says it was stripped and drops the game term shed.
The original says she caught the hare's cast. The rewrite says she found it and drops the game term catch.
The original says Rib lies west along the Midden Road. The rewrite says to start at Rib and then head west, which changes the direction.
The original says the fracture has come right up to the door. The rewrite says trouble has arrived and drops the game term fracture.
The original asks Ouro to move one step over to the side. The rewrite says one step back.
The original says his shell came off late. The rewrite says it came in late.
The original says the shop opens later because it is Shedding Day. The rewrite says Shedding Day itself opens soon.
The original calls Ouro a late one (someone whose shell has not come off) who must walk the Rim. The rewrite says "a late entry" and puts the Strandmonger on the walk with "we're taking".
The original says people who have shed walk behind their own shell. The rewrite says they walk in its shadow, which reads as an idiom about being overshadowed.
The original says Gran's slate (her tab) is long enough to take one more stray. The rewrite about a slate "worn long enough to bear the weight" reads as nonsense.
The original says Squall came off a sideways spring rain, so it is that rain's shell. The rewrite says it was caught in the rain.
The original says the whorl picked Ouro back in return. The rewrite says it chose Ouro again.
The original jokes that holding the Register costs a cowrie. The rewrite says storage costs a cowrie, which reads as a rule about the Midden.
The original says a weaker whorl makes a surer catch. The rewrite says less strength means better control, which changes the catch rule.
The original prices Knuckle's hands at a house each and calls the pearl cheap. The rewrite prices each pearl at a house and then calls the pearl cheap, which contradicts itself.
The rewrite says "The Tackle" and "it", which treats the whorl's name Tackle as an ordinary word.
The original says the Hermits take (seize) big whorls. The rewrite says they bring them.
The original says he will go and wait by the well. The rewrite says he will stay where he is.
The original means the pearl Knuckle gives out. The rewrite turns the name into a "knuckle-pearl".
The original notice names Ouro. The rewrite switches to "You acquire", unlike every other notice.
The original hands over the Rib pearl. The rewrite addresses Ouro as "Rib".
The original says you get tide from the small moves. The rewrite says from "subtle shifts", which no longer names the moves.
The original says Tack is still standing in the road. The rewrite invents being caught in a wind shadow.
The original says Leeward is one keeper against eleven Hermits. The rewrite says Leeward has one keeper.
The original tells the Hermits to let the Mast lean. The rewrite tells them to let a boat heel.
The original says Leeward's deck is to the north. The rewrite says the deck faces north.
The original has nacre caught in the drift. The rewrite says mother-of-pearl and drops the game term nacre.
The original says Grandad shed in the nave. The rewrite says he was buried there.
The original means stop the wind-up or take the hit. The rewrite turns it into a threat and loses the battle advice.
The original says rain falls upward near the Bole and carries hats up. The rewrite says the rain is strong and loses the upward rain the next line depends on.
The original says Tarhaju whorls drop fruit. The rewrite calls them rings and drops the game term whorl.
The original has a notion under the acorns. The rewrite says a secret and drops the game term notion.
The original says two nacre. The rewrite says two shells and drops the game term nacre.
The original says Grafton conjoins better than the Conjoiner. The rewrite says Grafton "meshes together" and the second sentence is garbled.
The original says his cast went up into the roots. The rewrite calls it his prosthetic.
The original says the Grafter made four whorls out of eight and misses two of the originals. The rewrite reads as a score of four out of eight.
The original says a whorl holds one notion each. The rewrite says the shop has one of each.
The original calls Ouro a late one. The rewrite says "a slow start".
The original says each of Grafton's four was two whorls and is now one. The rewrite says each was once split in two, which reverses it.
The original says to fight Grafton's whorls. The rewrite says to activate them.
The original says the Hermits went north to the machine fields and the town of Hum. The rewrite says Hum went with them.
The original is about a furnace cast. The rewrite drops cast and says a furnace.
The choice "No what?" becomes "What no?", which is garbled.
The original says the Pylon is going the way the Bole went. The rewrite says things are going as the Bole intended.
The original says arms in first. The rewrite says arms out first.
The original asks Ouro to turn around so Bare can see their back. The rewrite says "Face me", which is the opposite.
The letter is signed by Cinch. The rewrite reads the name as the verb "Tighten it".
The original says the Tusk should come out easily. The rewrite says the Hermits should take it easy.
The original says his grandmother's grandmother. The rewrite says great-grandmother, which is one generation short.
The original says his cast is ninety and twelve. The rewrite says his pension and that he is twelve.
Amber is the keeper's name. The rewrite says "The amber".
The original says Amber was right that she is a terror at fights. The rewrite says she was right to be concerned.
The original says the team fights to the worn pearl. The rewrite invents greater cohesion as the effect of a charm.
The original says Cinch came down to the Rim and went back up quieter. The rewrite names Ouro and reverses the direction.
The original says the late ones (people whose shell has not come off) should get a go. The rewrite says those who came in late.
The original says she shed the day she climbed down. The rewrite says she took it off and drops the game term shed.
The original says the cast never fought. The rewrite says it never resisted.
The original says wild conjoined whorls are on the road. The rewrite says "wild patterns".
The original greets Ouro as a late one. The rewrite says latecomer, which means someone who arrived late.
The original asks if Ouro is the late one. The rewrite says "late arrival", which means someone who arrived late at the Pylon.
The choice to catch the moon with a horn becomes "Grab it" and drops the game term catch.
The choice to fight it becomes "Resist".
Fall is a town name. The rewrite says "the Falls".
The original says to duel with the moon sent out. The rewrite says to duel with that horn.
The original means if the Seal lasts through the night. The rewrite says if it keeps the night out.
The original says keeper rematches are fought at level twenty-five. The rewrite says he fought at age twenty-five.
The original says both teams fight at level 25. The rewrite says both players.
The original challenges Ouro to a fight. The rewrite says try to argue.
The placeholder {#1} moves from the start of the line into the sentence as the thing Tack accepts.
The original foretells that Ouro will have looked at its hands. The rewrite gives an order and says Ouro will look back on the moment.
The original means Ouro coming up loose (their shell loosening). The rewrite says unprepared.
The original tells Ouro to look back down. The rewrite adds "Keep moving" while Bare is blocking the way.
The original says the fracture is a number of fingers long. The rewrite says fingers deep.
The original says Ouro is four spans tall and one span short of a Hand. The rewrite says four spans minus one hand's width.
The original says the air is close (muggy) in the room. The rewrite reads it as an order to pull in tight.
The original says owe it all again. The rewrite says pay it back in full.
The original says the Hands took orders from a habit (the cast at the post). The rewrite says they ran on autopilot.
The original says old shell and fractures. The rewrite says carcass and cracks and drops the game term fracture.
The original says she said a new one. The rewrite says she said there is a new one.
The original says the well's water is up to the top. The rewrite says the well is awake.
The original says they carry water from Rib. The rewrite says they haul the dust from Rib.
The original says the lost boot is the right one (right foot). The rewrite says the correct one and loses the clue.
The original says the meadow shed and grew over its cast. The rewrite makes a meadow shed a building and drops cast.
The original has a notion in the jar. The rewrite says powder and drops the game term notion.
The original asks if we are cold. The rewrite asks if you are freezing, which changes who.
The original says one nail shed and its shell follows her. The rewrite says the nail fell off and drops shed.
The original says the ship behaved in a seaworthy way. The rewrite says it conducts itself at sea.
The original says the sea's cast. The rewrite says the sea's casting.
The original says see you tomorrow and the roots too. The rewrite addresses "you two".
The original has a notion under the bark. The rewrite says a thought forms and drops the game term notion.
The original says Ouro keeps the bowl upside down. The rewrite says Ouro inverts it.
The original says he will not be the one to tell the swords. The rewrite says he won't pick one up.
The original says the war horses have been whorls for a hundred years. The rewrite says idle and drops the game term whorl.
The original has a notion in the pouch. The rewrite says a trinket and drops the game term notion.
The original says the soldier copies Ouro's steps the wrong way round. The rewrite says mirrors them but in reverse, which can read as the same way round and muddles the puzzle hint.
The original says the shell copies Ouro's steps the wrong way round. The rewrite says mirrors them but in reverse, which can read as the same way round and muddles the puzzle hint.
The original says things the water showed are lying about. The rewrite says the reflections are lies.
The original has a nautilus horn. The rewrite says a nautilus shell and drops the game term horn.
The original says "There I am" about her reflection. The rewrite says "Here I am".
The original has a notion beside the bell. The rewrite says an idea and drops the game term notion.
The original says Ouro lit the glass room. The rewrite says Ouro shattered it.
The original says every Hand wears her glove and she has never shaken one. The rewrite says she gloves every hand and none are shaken, which is garbled.
The original has a notion and a nautilus horn. The rewrite says an idea and a nautilus shell and drops both game terms.
Purchase is the name of a Hand. The rewrite says "my Purchase".
The original says cutting one tree makes its neighbors shed. The rewrite says they drop their leaves, which changes the puzzle hint.
The original says nobody drew the Blank into the map. The rewrite says nobody summoned it.
The leading comma becomes the literal text "[comma]".
The original tells the turnip about soup. The rewrite sends love to "my little turnip soup".
The original means come home on Sundays without exception. The rewrite says it's Sunday.
The original asks who is turning Ouro's post. The rewrite asks who is keeping watch at it.
The choice answers that Tack is turning the post. The rewrite says "Secure it" and drops the name Tack.
The original says this seat shows what Ouro came out of. The rewrite says what brought Ouro here.
The original says Cinch always taps his own foot in here. The rewrite asks Ouro to tap his foot.
The original says a tide bell turns the tide. The rewrite says it reverses the current.
The original says stars fall in a line at low tide. The rewrite says the stars align.
The original says a still shell is gone when the shadow passes. The rewrite says when its own shadow passes, which changes the rule.
The original has a notion in the weed. The rewrite says an idea and drops the game term notion.
The original says to get inside something at low water. The rewrite says to enter the water.
The original says the family is inside the whelk because it is low water. The rewrite says they are good to go and loses that they are inside.
The original letter is addressed to the inside of the Volute. The rewrite says "Dear reader" and loses who she writes to.
The original letter is addressed to the inside of the Volute. The rewrite says "Dear reader" and loses who she writes to.
The original says somebody finally read one of her letters. The rewrite begs someone to read one, which reverses it.
The original says the writer is nobody here. The rewrite says nobody here knows them.
The original says the Strandmonger keeps a shop counter in the east petal. The rewrite says he tracks a counter.
The original warns against breaking the Sand Dollar to get at the doves. The rewrite says break the bank.
The original says they came off the old shell. The rewrite says they arrived on it.
The original says your trader, meaning Ouro's Strandmonger. The rewrite says our trader.
The original says cowries are cheap off the wrack, as cheap as sand. The rewrite says the wrack and the sand are cheap.
The original says take her, meaning Small Gran. The rewrite says take it and swaps she to it.
The original says the road is worth more to Ouro than a cowrie and less to him. The rewrite compares it to a shell and is garbled.
The original says thirty stars earns a notion. The rewrite says a thought and drops the game term notion.
The original says Tack came through Ouro's hole. The rewrite says it went through.
The original says the cell holds a number of measures. The rewrite says that many were measured out.
The original says two of the Sifter's four whorls are salt. The rewrite says two of four components.
The original says the Sifter now has no house. The rewrite says the house is empty.
The original says the Sifter lost the house after two hours away. The rewrite says the Sifter gets two hours out of it and is garbled.
The original says there is room at the fire until the Sifter finds another house. The rewrite says until he finds someone else.
The original says anything less than two lows will not do. The rewrite says if it moves any less, which is garbled.
The original has a notion at the bottom. The rewrite says a thought takes shape and drops the game term notion.
The original says you see only inside star rings and soft sand shows in a ring. The rewrite drops only and soft, which changes the rule.
The original says a SALT whorl worn in the lead walks you through gray. The rewrite says worn smooth by the lead, which changes the rule.
The original says Gloss is the keeper of the mouth. The rewrite says Gloss keeps the mouth shut.
The original says your reflection is three steps behind you. The rewrite says three steps behind mine.
The original says the spots are on the Cowrie's back and to catch one. The rewrite says the back porch and grab one.
The original says a VOID whorl worn in the lead. The rewrite says carved into the lead, which changes the rule.
The original has a nautilus horn and a notion. The rewrite says a nautilus shell and an idea and drops both game terms.
The original says the speaker sits in the only gap in town. The rewrite says the speaker is the only gap.
The original means at every low water. The rewrite says at every low point.
The original means the light came in at low water. The rewrite says at the low point.
The original says the light came in at low water. The rewrite says it trickled in low and slow.
The original says Cinch came down when the stamping started. The rewrite says it started.
The original says when the tide rolls the Auger over. The rewrite says when the tide rolls in.
The original says pull the plug from the vent. The rewrite says disconnect the vent, which can read as closing it.
The original says plug the vent. The rewrite says connect the vent, which can read as opening it.
The original says to sound the vents in that order. The rewrite says to chant the sequence.
The original names the point, the Auger's tip. The rewrite says the goal.
The original says they will climb every low water. The rewrite says every rise.
The original says Tack is scratching the score in. The rewrite says scratching it, which can read as crossing it out.
The original says the voice is heard on the sandbar and that this morning was seventy years ago. The rewrite says in the bar and makes it an anniversary.
The original says she takes off her boot on the sandbar. The rewrite says in the bar.
